items.title: Unit tests pass
items.description: Verify isolated Seed-critical behavior through the repository test suite.
items.method: Run npm test from the repository root as the shared test producer.
evidence_required: Exact npm test command and exit status.
Complete passing summary or failing diagnostics from all test files.
Confirmation that fixture repositories and homes were disposable and cleaned.
items.evidence: @verifications.unit-tests re-reviewed after the intentional GitHub license genome catalog expansion. Its stored proof commands pass against the current revision; changed evidence files test/genomes.test.js remain consistent with this item and active global policies.

items.title: Repository README is accurate and safely executable
items.description: Verify @repo-readme contains the actual project entrypoint information, inventory every shell command, and use @seed-evidence-scripts to exercise safe real CLI paths only in disposable repository and user-home locations.
items.method: Reuse npm test as the shared test producer, then run node seed/scripts/verify-readme.js from the repository root. The verifier classifies every README shell command, rejects unknown command forms, and executes representative project, genome, verification, named-Seed, and skill-installation paths under a temporary repository, HOME, CODEX_HOME, and CLAUDE_HOME that it removes in a finally block. Network/global-install, placeholder, interactive pager, and terminal evidence-transition examples are inspected but not executed.
evidence_required: Exact npm test and README verifier commands with exit statuses.
Confirmation that repository files and real user skill homes were unchanged.
items.evidence: repo-readme inventories all 63 shell commands and executes both genome-search examples plus representative CLI paths in disposable repository and skill homes; npm test passes and real user locations remain untouched

### Contract Language

_Address: `behavior.contract-language` · Source: `seed/seed.yml`_

#### Document Model

_Address: `behavior.contract-language.document-model` · Source: `seed/seed.yml`_

A Seed is YAML with required metadata and nonempty scope, interfaces, behavior, constraints, freedom, and verifications sections; errors may be empty. Optional addressable sections are artifacts, state, security, environment, observability, and compatibility.

#### Metadata Tags

_Address: `behavior.contract-language.metadata-tags` · Source: `seed/seed.yml`_

Seed and genome metadata may include an optional tags field containing a simple list of nonempty strings. Tags preserve authored spelling and order and do not create contract addresses.

#### Address Normalization

_Address: `behavior.contract-language.address-normalization` · Source: `seed/seed.yml`_

Addressable trees and ID-bearing lists compile into unique dotted addresses. IDs start alphanumeric and contain only letters, numbers, underscores, and hyphens. Known item properties remain fields rather than child addresses.

#### Requirements Readiness

_Address: `behavior.contract-language.requirements-readiness` · Source: `seed/seed.yml`_

requirements is a temporary planning inbox. Blueprint and diff expose unresolved entries, but validation and verification start fail until it is absent or empty and the entries have been converted into the contract.

#### Artifacts And References

_Address: `behavior.contract-language.artifacts-and-references` · Source: `seed/seed.yml`_

Artifacts use repository-relative paths or HTTP(S) URLs and require descriptions. Items that mention local artifacts declare their IDs. Local, cross-Seed, and genome-qualified references must resolve or fail.

#### Policies

_Address: `behavior.contract-language.policies` · Source: `seed/seed.yml`_

Ordinary items default to local policy, security items default global, and explicit global policy items are supplied as context for every verification claim and checked by audit.

### Repository Selection

_Address: `behavior.repository-selection` · Source: `seed/seed.yml`_

#### Default And Named Seeds

_Address: `behavior.repository-selection.default-and-named-seeds` · Source: `seed/seed.yml`_

The default Seed is master. Named Seeds use safe non-master names and isolated authored and generated paths. Listing reports master first and then safe named Seeds in lexical order.

#### Initialization

_Address: `behavior.repository-selection.initialization` · Source: `seed/seed.yml`_

init validates requested genomes before writes, creates only the selected contract and scripts directory, refuses replacement unless --overwrite, and idempotently ignores only .seed/locks in a seed-lang gitignore block.

### Genomes

_Address: `behavior.genomes` · Source: `seed/seed.yml`_

**Artifacts:**
- genome-catalog
- github-license-template-catalog

#### Resolution

_Address: `behavior.genomes.resolution` · Source: `seed/seed.yml`_

Genome lookup precedence is built-in, user, then repository. Requested genomes compose in order and local Seed values merge last. The winning address retains origin, ID, and path provenance.

**Artifacts:**
- genome-catalog

#### Composition

_Address: `behavior.genomes.composition` · Source: `seed/seed.yml`_

Recursive composition detects cycles and excessive depth. Keyed objects merge recursively, ID arrays merge by ID, addressable tree/list forms normalize together, ordinary arrays replace, and scalars replace.

#### Selectors

_Address: `behavior.genomes.selectors` · Source: `seed/seed.yml`_

String and object selectors include sections, addresses, subtrees, or artifacts with reference and artifact closure. Exclusions remove exact, subtree, ID, artifact, or glob matches after composition. Any unmatched selector fails.

#### Complete Exclusion

_Address: `behavior.genomes.complete-exclusion` · Source: `seed/seed.yml`_

Standalone !genome exclusions are order-independent, remove the genome transitively throughout the composed graph, and fail when unmatched.

#### Search

_Address: `behavior.genomes.search` · Source: `seed/seed.yml`_

Genome search uses case-insensitive substring matching across definition IDs, metadata names, summaries or descriptions, tags, and direct authored address names. --full-text additionally searches values within each direct address. Built-in, user, and repository origin filters apply; deterministic results report each genome's ID, origin, tags, match types, and matching addresses without treating inherited addresses as direct matches.

#### Runtime Verification Cleanup

_Address: `behavior.genomes.runtime-verification-cleanup` · Source: `seed/seed.yml`_

Built-in deployment genomes that verify configurable runtime identities require unique disposable workspaces beneath /tmp for all mutable test data and bind-mount sources, reliable cleanup on success and failure, and post-cleanup proof that test containers, volumes, networks, directories, and files with test-selected ownership were not left behind.

**Artifacts:**
- genome-catalog

#### Repository License Selection

_Address: `behavior.genomes.repository-license-selection` · Source: `seed/seed.yml`_

The built-in repo-license-* selection genomes cover every standard template in @github-license-template-catalog. Each composes repo-license, selects one GitHub license key and reported SPDX identifier through shared contract addresses, requires matching LICENSE and repository metadata, and leaves the owner responsible for the legal choice.

**Artifacts:**
- genome-catalog
- github-license-template-catalog

#### Constructed Blueprint

_Address: `behavior.blueprints-and-diffs.constructed-blueprint` · Source: `seed/seed.yml`_

Blueprint compiles local and genome content into fixed semantic section order with exact addresses, values, references, provenance, applied genomes, filters, requirements readiness, and external dependencies.

#### Machine Data

_Address: `behavior.blueprints-and-diffs.machine-data` · Source: `seed/seed.yml`_

#### Cross Seed Dependencies

_Address: `behavior.blueprints-and-diffs.cross-seed-dependencies` · Source: `seed/seed.yml`_

Named-Seed and genome-qualified reference syntax resolves against another present compiled Seed, rejects self or missing targets, and enforces requested genome provenance. Referenced Seeds retain separate authority.

#### Drift

_Address: `behavior.blueprints-and-diffs.drift` · Source: `seed/seed.yml`_

Seed diff compares compiled YAML and Blueprint diff compares constructed semantics against the selected snapshot. Canonical dependency drift is reported separately and does not create or expire selected-Seed work.

### Verification

_Address: `behavior.verification` · Source: `seed/seed.yml`_

#### Work Queue

_Address: `behavior.verification.work-queue` · Source: `seed/seed.yml`_

Explicit verification items precede implicit items for addressable obligation sections. Claims have owners and leases; stale claims become reclaimable, ownership gates transitions, and terminal states are confirmed or failed.

#### Executable Evidence

_Address: `behavior.verification.executable-evidence` · Source: `seed/seed.yml`_

Confirm requires every command to pass; fail requires at least one to fail. Evidence uses existing unique repository-relative files, SHA-256 hashes, Seed-address fingerprints, bounded command diagnostics, and the selected repository as command working directory.

#### Expiry And Reconciliation

_Address: `behavior.verification.expiry-and-reconciliation` · Source: `seed/seed.yml`_

Missing or changed evidence, absent test commands, or changed referenced Seed addresses expire terminal evidence. New compiled items enter pending work and removed items leave the reconciled queue.

#### Replay And Refresh

_Address: `behavior.verification.replay-and-refresh` · Source: `seed/seed.yml`_

check executes each unique stored command once and fans results to all uses. refresh-expired is an atomic fast path only for confirmed, evidence-file-only expiry with no contract change or other pending work.

#### Completion And Sync

_Address: `behavior.verification.completion-and-sync` · Source: `seed/seed.yml`_

completed requires every item terminal; satisfied also requires no failed or expired items. sync requires satisfaction, advances current Seed and dependency snapshots, and preserves only still-valid terminal results.

## Error Semantics

### Unknown Subcommand

_Address: `errors.unknown-subcommand` · Source: `builtin:cli-subcommands`_

Unknown subcommands fail with a nonzero exit code and a helpful error message.

### Failure Exit Code

_Address: `errors.failure-exit-code` · Source: `builtin:cli-exit-codes`_

Every failure path exits with a nonzero exit code.

### Contract Input

_Address: `errors.contract-input` · Source: `seed/seed.yml`_

Missing contracts, malformed YAML, unsupported tags, invalid section shapes or IDs, unresolved requirements, bad artifact declarations, unresolved references, and invalid policies fail with contextual diagnostics.

### Repository Paths

_Address: `errors.repository-paths` · Source: `seed/seed.yml`_

Missing or non-directory --repo targets, missing or duplicate --seed, unsafe or reserved names, overwrite attempts, and missing snapshots fail without silently selecting another location.

### Genomes

_Address: `errors.genomes` · Source: `seed/seed.yml`_

Operations that load, compile, blueprint, or validate genomes fail for unknown or malformed definitions, malformed or unmatched selectors and exclusions, broken references, cycles, and recursion overflow with relevant genome or source context. Genome search rejects a missing query or unknown option. Genome listing and search may retain a malformed entry for an ID match while omitting unavailable metadata and address matches.

### Cross Seed References

_Address: `errors.cross-seed-references` · Source: `seed/seed.yml`_

Missing source Seeds or addresses, self-reference, and genome provenance mismatch fail without taking verification ownership of the source Seed.

### Verification

_Address: `errors.verification` · Source: `seed/seed.yml`_

Corrupt state, invalid transitions, wrong owners, missing or unsafe evidence, failed proof commands, incomplete audits, expiry, and unsatisfied sync fail visibly while retaining bounded command diagnostics where applicable.

### Skill Installation

_Address: `errors.skill-installation` · Source: `seed/seed.yml`_

Missing or conflicting platform choice, unsupported targets, missing bundled skill content, and filesystem replacement failures fail and preserve or restore the prior installation when replacement began.
